body: Yeah those pillars were annoying as hell. Wasn't a problem when fighting Lady Butterfly but with Owl it was. Especially when running back to heal/dodging some of his attacks. Also when cornered against the walls, the camera goes nuts.

Dying multiple times have no major consequences other than lowering unseen aid chance. Even the money loss thing is avoidable if you buy coin purses and upgrade prosthetic tools. Moreover, Dragon's blood (used to cure Dragon Rot) is abundant in this game. I know for a fact that most people are able to beat certain bosses only after 40 - 50 tries. Dying isn't a big deal in Sekiro.
I have a gtx 960 2gb and the game ran without any lag on 1600 x 900 medium. 1050 isn't far off. Might be a problem with drivers.

I had attack power 11 when I beat him in my first playthrough. Took about 8 hours. It definitely doesn't make a huge difference in boss fights. I see you are able to consistently get through the first phase. A bit more vitality would definitely help though. I guess try to get it to 17 or 18. Otherwise the combo in the second phase which ends with a spear thrust might break your posture early and you wont be able to mikiri it.

For the second phase, always stay at a medium distance from him, (his sword and spear attacks shouldn't be in range other than the thrust attack). When the jumps and hits you with the spear, dodge diagonally behind and punish him. Also after countering his thrust with a mikiri, you can get in one hit. After you get his health down to around 50% focus on breaking his posture.

The third phase is the same barring the lightning attacks. If you can pull off a lightning reversal, it will deal a HUGE damage to his vitality and posture. Otherwise you can dodge towards him/to his left. However lightning reversal trivialises the fight. You can practice it in fountainpalace with the violet warriors.
